records.name: Identifiability
records.summary: Distinct parameter values correspond to distinct distributions.
records.statistical_question_answered: Can the parameter be learned from the model distribution?
records.problem_addressed: Prevents meaningless estimation of indistinguishable parameters.
records.decision_improved: Improves model formulation in ANOVA and regression.
conditions_required: No two distinct parameter values give the same pmf/pdf.
guarantees: Parameter has a unique distributional meaning.
does_not_guarantee: It does not guarantee accurate estimation with finite data.
common_misuses: Estimating nonidentifiable parameters as if data can distinguish them.
diagnostic_questions: Do two parameter settings produce the same distribution?

records.name: Linear combination and contrast
records.summary: A weighted sum of parameters or statistics; a contrast has weights summing to zero.
records.statistical_question_answered: Which treatment comparison is being estimated or tested?
records.problem_addressed: Formalizes meaningful comparisons among ANOVA means.
conditions_required: For contrasts, weights sum to zero.
guarantees: Comparisons are invariant to common shifts.
does_not_guarantee: It does not choose scientifically meaningful contrasts automatically.
use_when: ANOVA treatment comparisons and simultaneous inference.
do_not_use_when: When weights do not correspond to a planned comparison.
common_misuses: Testing all pairwise differences without multiplicity control.
diagnostic_questions: Do weights sum to zero and match the question?

records.name: Prediction interval
records.summary: A random interval designed to contain an unobserved future random variable with specified probability.
records.statistical_question_answered: Where might a future observation fall?
records.problem_addressed: Separates prediction of observations from interval estimation of parameters or mean responses.
records.decision_improved: Improves regression reporting and uncertainty communication.
assumptions_required: Predictive model and future variable are specified.
guarantees: Coverage for the future observation is targeted.
does_not_guarantee: It is not the same as a confidence interval for the mean.
do_not_use_when: When extrapolating outside model support or observed x range without justification.
common_misuses: Using a mean confidence interval as a prediction interval.
diagnostic_questions: Is the target a parameter, mean response, or future observation?
checks_or_evidence_needed: Model, x0, variance estimate, prediction target.

records.plain_language_meaning: All treatment means are equal exactly when every contrast of the means is zero.
records.formal_statement_shape: θ1=...=θk iff Σa_iθ_i=0 for every a with Σa_i=0.
assumptions: Treatment mean vector θ is defined.
Contrasts have weights summing to zero.
conditions: Treatment mean vector θ is defined.
Contrasts have weights summing to zero.
records.conclusion: The classic ANOVA null can be expressed as a collection of contrast hypotheses.
records.why_it_matters: This connects ANOVA F tests to union-intersection logic.
records.proof_strategy_summary: One direction uses zero-sum weights; the other uses contrasts comparing individual means to a reference/average.

records.result_name: ANOVA F statistic from supremum of contrast tests

records.plain_language_meaning: Under the conditional normal regression model, least-squares estimators are normal with stated variances/covariance, independent of S², and scaled S² is chi-square.
records.formal_statement_shape: α̂,β̂ jointly normal; (n-2)S²/σ²~χ²_{n-2}; (α̂,β̂) independent of S².

conditions: Independent normal errors with common variance.
records.conclusion: Exact t/F confidence intervals and tests for regression parameters are available.

records.proof_strategy_summary: Express estimators as linear combinations of normal observations and apply quadratic-form independence.

what_breaks_if_assumptions_fail: Nominal size and coverage may fail.
